claims.statement: Lukasiewicz-PORT publicly offers specialized laboratory services to industry and research organizations, including commissioned work using advanced infrastructure.
Lukasiewicz-PORT describes simplified laboratory-service order forms and flexible, standards-based work models, evidencing an existing commercial service interface.
The EU RDI framework recognizes renting laboratories, supplying services to undertakings, and contract research as economic activities subject to applicable State-aid boundaries.

PCA accreditation is tied to a laboratory's current declared scope, methods, and activities, so method matching must bind the actual performing laboratory and current scope rather than the procurement network's brand.

EU State-aid rules generally require economic use of publicly supported research infrastructure to be priced at market or full cost plus an appropriate margin, with access on transparent and non-discriminatory terms.

J.S. Hamilton self-reports 6,500 daily samples, 8,600 active customers, and 2,600 accredited methods, while offering direct technical sales, quotations, sampling, and transport, evidencing demand but also a strong integrated incumbent.

Science Exchange and Scientist.com already market scientific-service sourcing, standardized intake, supplier matching, contracting, compliance, payments, and performance data across large provider networks.

contrary_evidence: Laboratories already sell directly, and public or accredited institutions may be unable or unwilling to grant reserved capacity or reseller terms.
PORT advertises simplified direct orders and dedicated technical support, while Hamilton and TUV Rheinland provide direct quotation and method-scoping assistance.
Science Exchange and Scientist.com already operate mature scientific-procurement orchestration platforms, although their disclosed focus is broader and often enterprise life sciences.
Publicly supported infrastructure may need transparent, non-discriminatory access and market or full-cost pricing, limiting exclusive or deeply discounted reservations.

economics.acquisition_route: Accounting and compliance advisers, e-commerce manufacturer groups, and search-driven fixed-scope testing menus
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Broker 500 projects annually by year 3 (unvalidated), build a Central European capacity network by year 7 (unvalidated), and support founder equity above PLN 5 million by year 8 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with laboratory scientists controlling technical methods
economics.gross_margin_basis: No owned instruments; standardized intake, sample logistics, and aggregated procurement support 45-62% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.payback: SME acquisition payback after 1-3 testing orders (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: 12-20% management spread on laboratory invoices (unvalidated) plus PLN 1000-3000 annual priority membership (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual compliance calendars (unvalidated) and recurring batch, supplier, or product tests

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reserved slots, turnaround history, method mapping, and repeat demand forecasts improve both availability and purchasing terms
fingerprint.customer: Polish hardware, materials, cosmetics, food, biotech, and industrial SMEs needing specialist tests
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Searchable fixed-scope menus and referrals from compliance advisers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Method-scoped laboratory procurement, reserved turnaround, sample custody, and comparable reports
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: SME pays when accepting a fixed-scope test package; laboratory is paid under the reserved-capacity agreement
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A buyer, regulator, certification plan, or product failure requires a specific laboratory result quickly

founder_fit: Technical specification matching suits an analytical founder.
Search and adviser channels minimize continuous networking.
The business can validate demand before purchasing equipment.
risks: Liability for sample custody or mismatched method scope.
Thin spread after laboratory and courier costs.
The stated PLN 75000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.
Misstating the network's own accreditation or using a report outside the performing laboratory's current scope.
Partner laboratories may prohibit resale, priority reservations, or customer-facing use of their names.
Direct laboratories and established procurement platforms may eliminate the intermediary spread.
Broad cross-industry coverage may require more technical support and relationship management than a part-time founder can provide.

structure.commercial_archetype: Reserved institutional-capacity wholesaler and managed testing procurement service
structure.control_point: Contracted laboratory slots, standardized intake methods, transparent accreditation scope, and cross-lab turnaround evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Laboratories must have authority to reserve commercial capacity, and SME demand must justify commitments without distorting accreditation or public-funding rules

thesis: Negotiate reserved, cancellable capacity and standardized service levels with accredited or otherwise clearly scoped Polish research laboratories, then sell SMEs complete sample-to-report testing packages. Partner labs perform and sign the work; the network controls procurement convenience, reserved slots, sample logistics, and comparable method metadata without implying its own accreditation.
title: LabSlot Procurement Network
uncertainties: Which tests have fragmented demand and painful enough procurement to support a spread?
Can capacity reservations be nonexclusive, cancellable, and compliant with each institution's rules?
Which laboratories will sign reseller, sample-custody, service-level, name-use, and liability terms?
What portion of target orders requires accredited results, and how often do buyers misunderstand the required method or scope?
Will SMEs pay a 12-20% spread or annual membership when direct labs already provide quotations and technical support?
What are actual quote-to-order conversion, repeat rate, turnaround variance, courier loss, retest, and refund costs?
Can adviser and search channels acquire customers with payback in 1-3 orders?
No reserved-capacity agreement, lab quote, customer interview, or paid order has been observed.
